entities.label: AgentObligationBinding
entities.rationale: An agent-obligation binding is an externally grounded specifically dependent continuant: it is a relational normative tie that inheres in an agent (bearer) in virtue of their standing within a legal or social institutional structure. This makes it a Role (BFO_0000023) rather than a Disposition, because its ground is external (the institutional/normative system) rather than intrinsic to the bearer. It is distinct from LegalObligation in that it emphasizes the binding relation between a specific agent and a specific obligation, but it is closely related. We mint it as a new class subsuming under BFO_0000023 and note its relation to the existing LegalObligation class.

relations.rationale: AgentObligationBinding is a kind of Role: an externally grounded specifically dependent continuant that inheres in an agent in virtue of institutional norms.
As a subclass of Role, it is also a specifically dependent continuant (BFO_0000020), inhering in exactly one bearer-agent.

open_questions: Is 'agent-obligation binding' intended as a dyadic relation between an agent and a norm, or as a role inhering solely in the agent? This affects whether it should be modeled as a Role (SDC on the agent) or as a relational quality/process.
Should AgentObligationBinding be a subclass of the existing LegalObligation class, or is it a distinct category (e.g., a meta-level binding that associates agents with obligation instances)?
Is the binding universal (applies to all agents in a system) or particular (a specific agent bound by a specific obligation)? If particular, individual rather than class may be more appropriate.
Does 'binding' here entail enforceability or mere normative attribution? This would affect whether a Disposition (capacity to be compelled) should also be modeled alongside the Role.
proposal.rationale_summary: An 'agent-obligation binding' describes the normative tie by which an agent is bound to a specific obligation within a legal or institutional framework. In BFO terms, this is best classified as a Role (BFO_0000023), a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in the agent-bearer and is externally grounded in the institutional/normative system. It is externally grounded (the obligation comes from outside the agent's intrinsic nature), which distinguishes it from a Disposition (BFO_0000016). The existing class LegalObligation (already typed as BFO_0000023) is related but represents the obligation itself, whereas AgentObligationBinding represents the relational binding of a particular agent to an obligation. We mint a new class AgentObligationBinding as a subclass of BFO_0000023. Several open questions remain about whether the binding is best modeled as a role, a relational quality, or a process, and whether it should be subordinated to LegalObligation.
